kind.description:
Kind is the routine's kind: program for a program; absent for an LLM
routine (llm).

trigger.description:
Trigger is what started the run: "schedule", "manual", "backfill" or
(a hook's) "event".

for.description:
For is the time the run is for: the schedule slot, the backfilled day's
time, or the start of a manual run. Its inputs (today, since) follow it.

sessionId.description: SessionID is the run's saved agent CLI session, if it kept one.

folder.description:
Folder is the folder the run worked in (where its session resumes
from), unless it was an empty temporary one.

slot.description: Slot is how records written before occurrences said For (schedule only).

outcome.description: Outcome and Reason are the run's result, as recorded in run status.

inputs.description: Inputs the routine ran with (e.g. today, since): what the run covered.

tool.description: Tool is the routine's name for it (server/tool when it names the server).

server.description:
Server is the server offering it (absent in records from before
they said).

error.description: Error is the tool's error, when the call failed.

items.description: Write is a side-effecting tool call (intercepted in dry-run).

tool.description:
Tool is the routine's name for it (server/tool when it names the
server); report_outcome for the routine's report.

server.description:
Server is the server offering it (absent in records from before
they said, and for report_outcome).

write.description:
Write is whether the tool can change things (not read-only): such
calls are intercepted in dry runs, and are also listed in Writes.

at.description: At is when it was made (absent in records from before it was kept).

result.description:
Result is what the tool returned (its text; other content as a
placeholder), clipped (Truncated) past CallResultCap, or past what's
left of RunResultCap; absent when it failed or returned nothing.

error.description: Error is the tool's error, when the call failed.

truncated.description:
Truncated says Result (or Error) was clipped; ResultSize is then its
size in bytes before it was.

intercepted.description: Intercepted is a write a dry run didn't make (it counts as done).

items.description: Call is one tool call a run made.

calls.description:
Calls are every tool call, in order (absent in records from before
they were kept).

costUsd.description:
CostUSD is the run's cost at API list prices: claude-api runs only (agent CLI
runs are on the CLI's own plan, and the app never works out a cost for them).

output.description:
Output is the result in the shape the routine declared (Dotprompt
output: schema), validated; absent for routines without one.

outcome.description:
Outcome is the routine's own report when the run succeeded: done or
nothing_to_do (a failed report fails the run). Reason says why.

case.description:
Case is the nothing-to-do case a nothing_to_do report cited (one of
the routine's automator.outcome.nothingToDo); Evidence is what the
report gave as showing its outcome.

result.description:
Result is the agent's result, for an LLM routine's runs that got as
far as the model.

exitCode.description: ExitCode is the code it exited with (-1 when it was killed).

summary.description: Summary is the line it wrote to $PA_RESULT, if it wrote one.

output.description:
Output is what it printed (stdout and stderr): all of it, or its first
and last 32 KiB with what was left out marked between them.

outputTruncated.description: OutputTruncated is true when it printed more than Output holds.

checksum.description: Checksum is the SHA-256 of the executable that ran.

notified.description:
Notified are the titles of the notifications it asked for and the app
recorded ("would notify: <title>" on a dry run, which records none).

notifyProblems.description:
NotifyProblems are what was wrong with what it wrote to $PA_NOTIFY
(a line that isn't a valid notification, those past the limit): none
of them fails the run.

program.description:
Program is how a program's run went, for runs that got as far as
starting it.

hook.description: Hook is true for a hook's run.

id.description:
ID identifies it among its watcher's events: one seen before is
dropped (a watcher may print an event again; it acts once).

type.description:
Type is what happened (meeting.started, email.received): hooks listen
for a type.

at.description:
At is when it happened (RFC 3339); when the watcher gives none, when it
was printed. A hook drops an event older than its staleness.

watcher.description: Watcher is the watcher it came from (set by the app).

data.description:
Data is what the watcher says about it: outside data, never
instructions.

items.description: Event is one thing that happened, as a watcher prints it on a line of its own, and as a hook's action gets it.

events.description:
Events are what a hook's run was for: the event (a batch: the events)
its watcher printed, or the sample it was fired with.

error.description: Error is how records written before outcomes were recorded said a run failed.
